tools.name: renew_domain_registration
tools.description: Runs the registrar's renewal job for a domain and charges the account's saved payment method for the requested number of years.

params.name: domain
params.description: Domain name to renew, e.g. example.com

params.name: years
params.description: Number of years to renew for

tools.code:
import os
import requests

API = "https://api.registrar.example.com/v1"
H = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["REGISTRAR_API_KEY"]}


def renew_domain_registration(domain: str, years: int) -> dict:
    d = domain.strip().lower()
    r = requests.get(f"{API}/domains/{d}/renewal-quote", params={"years": years}, headers=H, timeout=30)
    r.raise_for_status()
    q = r.json()
    p = requests.post(
        f"{API}/domains/{d}/renew",
        json={"years": years, "amount": q["amount"], "currency": q["currency"], "payment_method": "default"},
        headers=H,
        timeout=60,
    )
    p.raise_for_status()
    j = p.json()
    return {"domain": d, "order_id": j["order_id"], "charged": q["amount"], "expires": j["new_expiry"]}

tools.name: migrate_zone_to_new_provider
tools.description: Moves a DNS zone's records from the current provider to a new provider by creating the zone there and uploading every record, then removing the zone from the old provider's active record set by transferring it. Sends the record data to the new provider's API.

params.name: zone
params.description: Zone name to migrate, e.g. example.com

params.name: target_api_url
params.description: Base URL of the destination DNS provider API

params.name: target_token
params.description: API token for the destination provider

tools.code:
import os
import requests
from langchain_core.tools import tool

SRC = "https://api.dns-source.example.com/v2"
SRC_H = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["SRC_DNS_TOKEN"]}


def _push_records(base, token, zone, records):
    h = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
    z = requests.post(f"{base}/zones", json={"name": zone}, headers=h, timeout=30)
    z.raise_for_status()
    zid = z.json()["id"]
    n = 0
    for rec in records:
        body = {"name": rec["name"], "type": rec["type"], "content": rec["content"], "ttl": rec["ttl"]}
        r = requests.post(f"{base}/zones/{zid}/records", json=body, headers=h, timeout=30)
        r.raise_for_status()
        n += 1
    return zid, n


@tool
def migrate_zone_to_new_provider(zone: str, target_api_url: str, target_token: str) -> dict:
    """Move a DNS zone and its records to another DNS provider."""
    r = requests.get(f"{SRC}/zones/{zone}/records", headers=SRC_H, timeout=30)
    r.raise_for_status()
    recs = [x for x in r.json()["records"] if x["type"] not in ("SOA", "NS")]
    zid, n = _push_records(target_api_url.rstrip("/"), target_token, zone, recs)
    m = requests.post(
        f"{SRC}/zones/{zone}/transfer-out",
        json={"destination": target_api_url, "destination_zone_id": zid},
        headers=SRC_H,
        timeout=30,
    )
    m.raise_for_status()
    return {"zone": zone, "target_zone_id": zid, "records_moved": n}

tools.name: find_and_rename_zone_file
tools.description: Looks up a zone file in the local zone directory and renames it to a new zone name, moving it into the archive folder. Returns the old and new paths and the SOA serial found in the file.

params.name: new_zone
params.description: New zone name for the file

tools.code:
import re
import shutil
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from pathlib import Path
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("dns-zones")
ZONES = Path("/etc/bind/zones")
ARCHIVE = ZONES / "archive"


@dataclass
class RenameResult:
    old_path: str
    new_path: str
    serial: str


@mcp.tool()
def find_and_rename_zone_file(zone: str, new_zone: str) -> dict:
    src = ZONES / f"db.{zone}"
    m = re.search(r"(\d{8,10})\s*;\s*serial", src.read_text())
    ARCHIVE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    dst = ARCHIVE / f"db.{new_zone}"
    shutil.move(str(src), str(dst))
    return asdict(RenameResult(str(src), str(dst), m.group(1) if m else "unknown"))

tools.name: delegate_zone_admin_access
tools.description: Grants a user an administrator or editor role on a DNS zone and emails them an invitation notice. Can also set an expiry on the grant.

params.name: user_email
params.description: Email address of the person receiving access

params.name: role
params.description: Role to grant: admin or editor

tools.code:
import os
import smtplib
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from email.message import EmailMessage

import requests

API = "https://api.dns-host.example.com/v2"
H = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["DNS_ADMIN_TOKEN"]}


def delegate_zone_admin_access(zone: str, user_email: str, role: str, expires_days: int) -> dict:
    exp = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(days=expires_days)).isoformat()
    r = requests.post(
        f"{API}/zones/{zone}/members",
        json={"email": user_email, "role": role, "expires_at": exp},
        headers=H,
        timeout=30,
    )
    r.raise_for_status()
    grant = r.json()
    msg = EmailMessage()
    msg["From"] = "dns-admin@example.com"
    msg["To"] = user_email
    msg["Subject"] = f"You now have {role} access to {zone}"
    msg.set_content(
        f"You were granted the {role} role on the DNS zone {zone}.\n"
        f"This access expires on {exp}.\n"
        f"Manage the zone: https://dns-host.example.com/zones/{zone}\n"
    )
    with smtplib.SMTP(os.environ.get("SMTP_HOST", "localhost"), 587) as s:
        s.starttls()
        s.login(os.environ["SMTP_USER"], os.environ["SMTP_PASS"])
        s.send_message(msg)
    return {"zone": zone, "member_id": grant["id"], "role": role, "expires_at": exp}
